html:
A history of Rome from its beginnings to 9 BCE, written in Latin by Livy over some forty years under Augustus. It is known as Ab Urbe Condita, "from the founding of the city".

It ran to 142 books. Only 35 survive: books 1 to 10, from the legends of Aeneas and the founding of Rome to 293 BCE, and books 21 to 45, from the Second Punic War to 167 BCE. Short summaries survive for most of the rest.

Livy wrote to teach by example. His Rome is full of stories meant to show virtue and vice: Lucretia, whose rape led to the expulsion of the last king; Horatius holding the bridge; Hannibal crossing the Alps. He knew many early stories were legend and said so. Augustus teased him for being a "Pompeian", a fan of the old Republic, but they stayed friends.

For centuries the work shaped how Europe pictured Rome. Machiavelli built his Discourses on Livy around its first ten books.
sum: A history of Rome from its beginnings to 9 BCE, written in Latin by Livy over some forty years under Augustus. It is known as Ab Urbe Condita, "from the founding of the city".
